incidental_findings.finding: 'Look at the 4x3 array. How many squares are shaded in all?' never says all squares are shaded, yet the key assumes full shading. Seed 103 says explicitly 'Shade ALL the squares', so the generator family does distinguish partial from full - if any array item renders a partially shaded grid the key is wrong.

Factor-role convention flips between item types. Numeral items write (size of group) x (number of groups) - 2 jumps of 3 -> '3 x 2'. Array items use rows x columns - '2x4 array. It shows 4 + 4'. Products are unaffected so no key is wrong, but at the exact grade where the array should GROUND the multiplication sentence, multiplicand and multiplier swap roles depending on the model.

Four of ten items contain no multiplication at all: three are pure square-counting and one is bare addition with no x, no groups language, and no model. None reaches the 'as multiplication' bridge that is the point of the competency.
The option '1' appears three times and corresponds to no plausible pupil error in repeated addition.

The fact 3 x 2 = 6 appears four times (40% of the sample) and the answer '6' is the key four times. The only factors used anywhere are 2, 3 and 4 - no 5s and no 10s. Every item runs model/addition -> product; nothing runs picture -> multiplication sentence.
All arithmetic verified correct; no second option correct; no vocabulary or operation exceeds the grade.
